ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a vertical large rectangle, divided into several squares. On the left side of the bottom there are three small squares side by side, and inside each small square is marked “1”. Above these three small squares is a larger square; on the right side of the bottom is another even larger square; at the very top there is also a large square spanning the entire width of the rectangle. Reasoning: The problem says the areas of the three smallest squares are each 1, so the side length of each smallest square is 1. The three smallest squares on the left side of the bottom are arranged horizontally, so their combined width is 1+1+1=3. The square directly above them has the same width as these three small squares combined, so the side length of this square is 3. The height of the lower-right square is equal to the overall height of the lower-left part, that is, the upper square with side length 3 plus the lower small square with side length 1, so the total height is 3+1=4, therefore the side length of the lower-right square is 4. The topmost square spans the entire width of the rectangle, and its width is equal to the lower-left part width 3 plus the lower-right square width 4, namely 3+4=7, so the side length of the topmost square is 7. The width of the entire large rectangle is 7, and the height is the upper square's 7 plus the lower part's 4, namely 11. Therefore the area of the large rectangle is 7×11=77.
